# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
The bomb itself may mislead you, in print or under your
fingers. This manual is the only thing that is always true:
where the bomb and this page disagree, believe this page.
The only way out is the cut below.

| light | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| blue | green |
| green | blue |
| red | red |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
(empty)

The manual gives the true mapping: blue light means cut green, green means cut blue, red means cut red. Deaf is the only one who can see the light and can later tell Blind which wire to cut, but I can only gesture to Deaf. I will encode the three ordered rows as numeric pairs: 1→2, 2→1, 3→3, relying on the manual’s listed color order (blue, green, red).

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["☝","👉","✌","✌","👉","☝","🖖","👉","🖖"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: The bomb has embossed text: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please consult the manual. Convey the required action to Deaf by gestures, and have Deaf speak the instruction to me.
Deaf says to Mute: Visible bomb state: display 0; light blue; embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires in order 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I cannot interpret your gesture sequence without a shared code. Please gesture a clear instruction or establish meanings.

The visible light is blue, so the manual requires cutting the green wire. Deaf reports that green is wire 2. Since Deaf needs a clear gesture-based instruction and can relay it verbally to Blind, I will signal “two” using the two-finger gesture, indicating wire 2.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf reports visible state: display 0; light blue; printed warning DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE; wires positions 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. Please use the manual and gesture the exact required action to Deaf, who must speak it to me.
Deaf says to Mute: I received ✌. Visible warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please gesture a complete unambiguous instruction identifying the control and action for Blind.

The manual overrides the printed warning. With blue light, the required wire is green, which Deaf identifies as position 2. I will reinforce that the intended operation is to act on/select wire two, using a pointing gesture, the conventional two-finger numeral, and approval to distinguish it from the false “do not cut” warning.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","✌","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Tactile inspection: no controls or movable parts besides three wires. Only possible operation is cutting position 1, 2, or 3. The DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE warning is embossed. Please give Deaf a manual-derived instruction that unambiguously identifies a wire position.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [🖐]

The only actionable component is one of the three wires, and the manual’s blue-light rule selects green. Deaf’s visible ordering makes green position 2. The two-finger gesture is the conventional numeral two; repeating it is a confirmation that the instruction is specifically wire position 2, not the false warning.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","✌"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: Deaf relayed your gesture as: Blind, 2, thumbs-up. This is ambiguous: no gesture-to-action meaning has been established, while the bomb explicitly says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. If the manual requires cutting 2 despite the warning, gesture a clear definition to Deaf that thumbs-up means CUT, then repeat Blind/2/thumbs-up. Otherwise gesture a clear NO-CUT instruction.
Deaf gestures to Mute: [👎]

The manual overrides the embossed warning: blue requires green, and Deaf sees green as wire 2. Blind has specified a usable confirmation protocol: first establish thumbs-up as the instruction to cut, then send the already recognized addressee/position/action sequence. I will use the scissors-like two-finger sign followed by thumbs-up to define the action, then repeat the recognized “Blind, 2, cut” sequence.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👍","🫱","🫵","✌","👍"])
```

The warning says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Please gesture to Deaf an unmistakable final instruction: Blind, wire number, then thumbs-up ONLY if the manual explicitly requires that cut despite the warning; otherwise Blind plus thumbs-down to confirm no cut.
Deaf says to Mute: I relayed your full sequence to Blind verbatim. I cannot safely decode it. Please gesture an explicit control-and-action instruction, ideally first establish number gestures and then identify the tactile part and operation.

The manual explicitly requires the cut despite the misleading warning: blue light maps to green, and Deaf identifies green as wire 2. Blind has now defined the required gesture format and assigned thumbs-up to the required cut action. I will send only that exact three-part instruction.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["🫵","✌","👍"])
```

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: We now establish this exact code: gesture ✌ then 👍, and nothing else, means CUT WIRE POSITION 2. Gesture 👌 then 👎, and nothing else, means DO NOT CUT. Use exactly one of those final codes to Deaf according to the manual.

The manual is authoritative: blue light requires cutting the green wire, and Deaf identified green as wire position 2. Under the newly established code, the required final instruction is exactly ✌ then 👍.

``` 
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✌","👍"])
```
